issues.description: Buffer is an unbounded list; a long pre-connect stall can grow memory without limit.
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is a plain list with no cap. If a job hangs before init_recording or crashes slowly under heavy logging, every record stays resident. Data dominates: pick a bounded deque(maxlen=N) so the structure itself enforces the policy and the algorithm (append, drain) stays trivial.

issues.description: Replay walks root handlers searching for the OTLP LoggingHandler instead of holding a reference.
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer imports LoggingHandler inside the function and scans logging.getLogger().handlers to find the one _setup_cloud_tracer just added. The setup code knows exactly which handler it installed; pass or store it. The scan is fragile if multiple LoggingHandlers exist and is more code than the job warrants.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry mutates global root logger handlers as a side-effect of a deadlock workaround.
issues.detail: Removing every LoggingHandler from the root logger inside _shutdown_telemetry couples telemetry shutdown to global logging state and will silently drop handlers a user added themselves. The cleaner shape: keep a reference to the handler installed by _setup_cloud_tracer and detach only that one. Same data-structure point: track what you own.

issues.description: Four near-parallel lifecycle methods on JobContext could collapse into one buffer object.
issues.detail: _start_log_buffering, _stop_log_buffering, _flush_early_log_buffer, plus the _on_cleanup branch all manage one handler. A small LogBuffer object owning attach/detach/replay would be a struct-with-three-functions and remove the _early_log_handler None-dance from JobContext. Composition over scattered private methods.

issues.description: Disabling pytest-xdist and skipping a test file are unexplained collateral changes.
issues.detail: The makefile drops -n auto and removes test_plugin_google_stt.py from the unit-tests target. Neither relates to log buffering. If parallel runs became flaky because of the new global logger mutations, that is a real signal worth a comment; if not, this belongs in a separate PR. Don't smuggle test-infra changes through a feature diff.

issues.description: Reordering _queue_msg after pending-assignment registration is a load-bearing fix with no note.
issues.detail: worker.py now registers wait_assignment before sending availability_resp, closing a race where the server replies before the future exists. This is the right shape, but it is buried in an unrelated PR with no comment. A one-line comment ("register before send to avoid losing the assignment") would keep the next reader from undoing it.

review.summary: The crash-log upload path is the right idea — buffer early, replay once OTLP is wired, flush on cleanup — but the data structure is doing too little work. An unbounded list, a handler discovered by scanning the root logger, and four private lifecycle methods on JobContext add up to more moving parts than the problem deserves. A small LogBuffer owning its handler and a bounded deque would let the algorithm disappear. Also: the makefile and worker.py changes are unrelated and undocumented; split them or comment them.
